title: Pass or fail?
brief:
Ask the user for a mark with input(). If the mark is 40 or more, print pass. If it is less than 40, print fail.

One more thing: people make mistakes. If the user types something that is not a number, such as forty, do not crash. Print this instead:

```
Please type a number.
```

vocabulary.gloss: a question that is True or False, like mark >= 40
run one block of code when the condition is True, another when it is False
checking that the input is what you expected, before you use it
asks a string: are you only made of digits 0–9? Gives True or False

starterCode:
# Ask for a mark. Print pass (40 or more) or fail (less than 40).
# If the input is not a number, print: Please type a number.

mark = input("Mark: ")
hints: First check the input is a number. The text you got from input() has a method for this: mark.isdigit() is True if every character is a digit. Put your if around that.
Only after the check is it safe to use int(mark). Then compare: if int(mark) >= 40: print pass, else print fail.
The shape is two ifs, one inside the other. if mark.isdigit(): (indented) if int(mark) >= 40: print("pass") else: print("fail") — and an else on the outer if that prints Please type a number.
